def kth_largest(nums: list[int], k: int) -> int:
    """
    Returns the k-th largest element in an unsorted list using the Heap algorithm.
    Time complexity: O(n + k log n).
    """
    
    import heapq
    
    # Create a min-heap with the first k elements
    min_heap = nums[:k]
    heapq.heapify(min_heap)
    
    # Process the remaining elements
    for num in nums[k:]:
        if num > min_heap[0]:  # Only consider elements larger than the smallest in the heap
            heapq.heappop(min_heap)  # Remove the smallest
            heapq.heappush(min_heap, num)  # Push the new number onto the heap
            
    return min_heap[0]  # The root of the min-heap is the k-th largest element

def kth_largest(nums: list[int], k: int) -> int:
    """
    Returns the k-th largest element in an unsorted list using a modified
    binary search approach. Time complexity: O(n) on average, O(n^2) in worst case.
    """
    
    def count_greater_than(mid: int) -> int:
        """Count how many numbers are greater than mid."""
        return sum(num > mid for num in nums)

    left, right = min(nums), max(nums)

    while left < right:
        mid = left + (right - left) // 2
        count = count_greater_than(mid)

        if count < k:  # We need a larger value
            right = mid
        else:  # We can look for a larger mid
            left = mid + 1

    return left if count_greater_than(left) >= k else left - 1
